evidence: Wikipedia's article on Nile Rodgers: he produced David Bowie's 'Let's Dance' (1983), Bowie's most commercially successful album.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Listen to the guitar on both. On 'Good Times' Rodgers plays short, clipped, choppy chords, more rhythm than melody, locked to the drums. On 'Let's Dance' the same kind of guitar sits under Bowie's voice, along with a big, booming drum sound and horn stabs. It is Bowie borrowing a disco band's rhythm section to make a pop record.

explanation.age13: In 1983 David Bowie asked Nile Rodgers of Chic to produce his album 'Let's Dance'. It became the biggest-selling record of Bowie's career.
explanation.adult: A production edge that took Chic's dance-band discipline into 1980s rock-pop at the moment disco itself was out of fashion. It makes Rodgers a hinge between the funk and rock lanes, and it anticipates his Madonna work a year later.
